points.why: Says the vague instruction gave the agent nothing it could fail, and recommends a numbered checklist of concrete items such as page limits, font, budget justification and headings.
Flags that we don't know which chapters, appendices or attachments the agent opened, and requires per-chapter reports with locations, but never says to build the inventory from the proposal itself.
Treats 'all comply' as unevidenced, and has people spot-check the agent's quotes and confirm high-risk items against the funder's own wording.
Adds scripted checks for mechanical rules and attachment presence, plus cross-checks of budget figures against the narrative, which reading the text can't catch.

pitfalls.why: The rerun it proposes uses deliberately planted violations to test the checker, not the same vague check or an 'are you sure' prompt.
